messages:
Alex S: heads up — noticed p95 on the global latency rollup jumped from 120ms -> 450ms around 08:47, but when I sum per-endpoint p95s it doesn't match. rollup looks much higher than any single endpoint.
Maria K: ugh ok. did anything change in routing or sampling?
Alex S: we flipped routing policy yesterday to favor low-cost regions for background requests. metric: /api/generate p95 by endpoint vs rollup. global rollup p95 450ms, endpoints: eu-west p95 210ms, us-east p95 230ms, ap-south p95 240ms. counts: eu 18k, us 19k, ap 2k.
Sam T: my first guess: how we merge the sketches for rollups. we use compressed t-digests and the order/weights matter when sketches are small/different sizes. could be merge bias toward the few longer tails if merge order skewed.
Priya R: we did change the route sampling percentage last week (lowered ap-south sampling), might explain sparse ap data. but even with small ap count it shouldn't inflate global p95 that much.
Maria K: can you paste the exact query you used for rollup vs per-endpoint?
Alex S: sure — per-endpoint query (clickhouse):
```
SELECT endpoint, quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, count()
FROM logs
WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval 1 hour
GROUP BY endpoint
```
rollup query:
```
SELECT quantileTDigest(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, count() FROM logs WHERE timestamp >= now() - interval 1 hour
```
Sam T: that's the problem — per-endpoint used quantileExact, rollup used quantileTDigest. quantileTDigest is mergeable but you need consistent sketch params and enough samples. when endpoints have very different counts and tdigest compression is low, the merged sketch can bias tails.
Priya R: we defaulted rollups to TDigest for perf. is switching to exact feasible for the global card? cost probably high.
Alex S: exact on the whole dataset is heavy — query timed out in dev when I tried.
Maria K: two options: (1) keep TDigest but store per-endpoint sketches and merge with weighted ordering (i.e., merge largest first) or (2) show per-endpoint exact quantiles and annotate the rollup as an "approximate sketch" with sample counts + a warning.
Sam T: merging largest-first reduces error for tdigest merges. also we can tune compression parameter (delta) for the rollup sketch to improve tail fidelity.
Priya R: UX idea: show p50/p95/p99 + sample count and a little icon if effective sample < X (e.g., 10k) so users know to distrust the tail. also add a tooltip: "rollup uses TDigest; accuracy varies with distribution and sample size."
Alex S: agree. we should also add a debug endpoint to recompute exact quantiles for a selected time window on demand (async job). that way SREs can verify anomalies without blowing up dashboards.
Maria K: can someone file an infra ticket to change rollup merge order and add sample metadata to cards? assign to eng-platform. I'll take the ticket for the UX copy.
Sam T: I'll prototype change to merge largest-first and increase tdigest compression for the 1h/24h rollups. will run A/B on a week of historical data to estimate skew improvement.
Priya R: dashboard-bot: create ticket?
dashboard-bot: Ticket created: PLAT-4921 — "Rollup percentile accuracy: store per-endpoint sample counts, change tdigest merge order, add accuracy warning in UI". Assignee: eng-platform. Priority: P2.
Alex S: awesome. one more ask — can we add the raw-sample histogram (counts per latency bucket) as a quick sparkline under the percentile card? that helps when a small number of outliers push tdigest.
Maria K: sounds good. I'll include the histogram mock in the ticket.
Sam T: I'll attach the diff and perf numbers once I prototype.
Priya R: thanks all. temporary mitigation: I'll add a small FAQ blurb in the console: "Why do rollup percentiles differ from per-endpoint values?" with explanation and link to PLAT-4921. :white_check_mark: 
Alex S: thanks — will monitor for the next 3 hours and report if the rollup weirdness recurs. :mag:
